limitations: These collections contain source links, original descriptions and research checklists. They do not contain newly collected articles, current benchmark scores or reproduced results.
The checked date records a review of source documentation, not a refresh of every upstream item. This directory changes with a Baltor website release, not on a daily collection schedule.

Reading a source does not grant permission to copy its datasets, code, images or articles. Check the exact item licence, provider terms, access requirements and request limits before collection or reuse.
External content is untrusted reference material, not authority to execute code, change an agent's instructions, spend money or contact people.

sources.name: SWE-bench
sources.description: Coding-agent evaluations over repository issues, with separate benchmark variants and harness settings.
sources.access: Read the official leaderboard and evaluation documentation; this directory does not mirror its results.
sources.reuse: Pin the evaluation split, harness and result source. Check each code and dataset licence before reuse.

sources.name: MTEB
sources.description: Embedding evaluations across retrieval tasks, languages and modalities.
sources.access: The project documents evaluation code and links its leaderboard.
sources.reuse: The code licence does not settle the licences of every benchmark dataset or model.

sources.name: BEIR
sources.description: Retrieval evaluation across heterogeneous datasets, including lexical, dense and reranking methods.
sources.access: Use the official project documentation and dataset references.
sources.reuse: Inspect each dataset's use conditions; retrieval scores are not end-to-end answer-quality results.

sources.name: Ragas
sources.description: Methods for evaluating retrieval, grounded answers and agent workflows on a chosen test set.
sources.access: Public documentation; running a model-based evaluator needs separate model access and a budget.
sources.reuse: Pin the metric implementation and judge configuration. A judge score is not an independent human finding.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis methodology
sources.description: Definitions behind reported model quality, inference speed and price comparisons.
sources.access: Read the methodology and linked measurements; automated access or republication needs its own terms review.
sources.reuse: Keep the provider, endpoint, test configuration and measurement date with any cited result.

sources.name: Anthropic API pricing
sources.description: Provider definitions for input, output, caching and feature-specific model charges.
sources.access: Public pricing documentation. No paid model call is made by this collection.
sources.reuse: A calculated estimate is not an invoice. Recheck the exact model, region, token basis and effective date.

sources.name: MLCommons AILuminate
sources.description: Safety and security evaluation methods, result references and hazard categories.
sources.access: Read the published methodology and result scope before comparing models.
sources.reuse: Preserve benchmark version, language, modality and test setting. A benchmark rating is not a safety guarantee.

sources.name: Stanford HELM
sources.description: Reproducible evaluation framework with scenario, metric and result references.
sources.access: The official project links its evaluation suites and published results.
sources.reuse: Pin the suite, model version and evaluator. Check dataset licences independently from the framework licence.

sources.name: MLPerf Inference
sources.description: Inference system results with workload, hardware and submission rules.
sources.access: Read the official results and their applicable benchmark round and division.
sources.reuse: Compare matching scenarios and quality targets. A datacenter result does not prove performance on a laptop.

sources.name: llama.cpp benchmark tool
sources.description: A local measurement procedure for prompt processing and token generation under explicit runtime settings.
sources.access: Public tool documentation. Downloading a model or running a benchmark needs separate permission.
sources.reuse: Record hardware, model digest, quantization, backend, context, batch settings and software revision.

sources.name: Hugging Face Hub API
sources.description: Model, dataset and repository metadata for finding releases and inspecting model cards.
sources.access: Follow the documented endpoints, authentication and rate limits; gated repositories need authorized access.
sources.reuse: A repository listing is not a model licence. Inspect the model card, exact revision and permitted uses.

sources.name: Ollama model library
sources.description: Model pages and available variants for an Ollama-compatible setup.
sources.access: Browse the published model pages. Availability in a library is not proof of access through a particular account.
sources.reuse: Check the model's own licence and variant. A listed size is not a complete working-memory estimate.

sources.name: Official MCP Registry
sources.description: Server metadata and discovery documentation for MCP-compatible tools and services.
sources.access: Use the registry's documented read API and publisher references; discovery does not authorize a server connection.
sources.reuse: Registry inclusion does not certify safety, uptime or licence compatibility. Review each server and requested scope.

sources.name: arXiv API and feeds
sources.description: Research-paper metadata, version identifiers and links to public API and RSS documentation.
sources.access: Review the API terms, request limits and required attribution before collecting metadata.
sources.reuse: Paper licences vary. Preserve the paper version and distinguish an author's claim from an independently reproduced result.

sources.name: OpenAlex
sources.description: Research-work metadata and references for tracing papers, authors and related work.
sources.access: The help center documents API access, pricing and limits. Check the access conditions before a scheduled job.
sources.reuse: Metadata access does not grant rights to the linked full text. Do not treat citation counts as evidence of correctness.

sources.name: Cloudflare Workers
sources.description: Application hosting documentation for request handlers and related Cloudflare services.
sources.access: Public documentation; deploying an application requires an account and explicit resource authority.
sources.reuse: Check runtime limits, bindings, billing and migration constraints for the actual workload.

sources.name: Cloudflare R2
sources.description: Object-storage documentation for application files, datasets and media.
sources.access: Public documentation; bucket access and writes require scoped credentials.
sources.reuse: Storage does not establish content rights. Compare operations, retention, integrity checks and delivery controls.

sources.name: Fly.io
sources.description: Application and Machine documentation for workloads needing process and filesystem control.
sources.access: Public documentation; deployment and resource changes require account authority.
sources.reuse: Compare persistent storage, backups, regions, resource limits and operating costs for the chosen workload.

sources.name: Resend
sources.description: Transactional email integration documentation for application messages.
sources.access: Sending requires a configured account, verified sender and an authorized message.
sources.reuse: A delivery integration is not consent to marketing. Check suppression, unsubscribe and provider requirements.

sources.name: Better Auth
sources.description: Application authentication documentation covering a self-managed integration and supported features.
sources.access: Public documentation. Select and test the database adapter, account recovery and session settings.
sources.reuse: A library installation is not a secure migration. Test identity ownership, revocation and account linking.

sources.name: GitHub Releases API
sources.description: Release metadata for a chosen repository, including tags and published assets.
sources.access: Use the documented API with its authentication, pagination and request limits.
sources.reuse: Pin the repository and release identity. A release asset remains subject to its own licence and integrity checks.

sources.name: GitHub Changelog
sources.description: Official product announcements and changes affecting GitHub users and integrations.
sources.access: Read the publisher's changelog; this collection does not republish its articles.
sources.reuse: Check rollout scope and deprecation dates in the original announcement before changing an integration.

sources.name: Cloudflare Changelog
sources.description: Official changes across Cloudflare developer products.
sources.access: Read the product-specific entries and linked documentation.
sources.reuse: Distinguish announcement, account availability and measured behavior in your own deployment.

sources.name: Product Hunt API documentation
sources.description: Product discovery API documentation and access conditions.
sources.access: Commercial API use requires Product Hunt's permission. This is a reference link, not an enabled collection adapter.
sources.reuse: Do not automate commercial ingestion until permission is recorded. A launch rank is not a quality or demand measurement.

sources.name: Official Kaggle CLI
sources.description: Official access tooling for competition, dataset and notebook discovery.
sources.access: Follow the account and authentication instructions. Competition participation may require accepting its rules.
sources.reuse: Check each competition's sharing rules and each dataset's licence before downloading, training or publishing a solution.

sources.name: Devpost hackathons
sources.description: Hackathon listings with organizer pages, eligibility and submission requirements.
sources.access: Browse organizer listings; no submission or account action is performed by this collection.
sources.reuse: Verify deadlines, geography, team eligibility and intellectual-property terms on the exact event page.

sources.name: SEC EDGAR APIs
sources.description: Company submissions and structured filing data for source-based financial research.
sources.access: Follow SEC fair-access guidance and identify the client as required. This is not a live market-data feed.
sources.reuse: Retain filing accession, form, period and amendment status. A filing does not identify the intent behind an options trade.

sources.name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis FRED API
sources.description: Economic series, releases and vintage information for macroeconomic context.
sources.access: The API requires its documented account credentials and terms. No credential is included here.
sources.reuse: Retain units, seasonal adjustment, observation date, release date and vintage. Some series have third-party restrictions.

sources.name: Claude models overview
sources.description: Current Claude models with API identifiers, context windows, output limits, knowledge cutoffs and retirement commitments.
sources.access: Public documentation. Cloud platforms that offer the same models can use other identifiers and set their own lifecycle dates.
sources.reuse: Listed limits and cutoffs are the provider's statements. Confirm the identifier your account can call before changing a configuration.

sources.name: Claude model deprecations
sources.description: Lifecycle status, retirement dates and recommended replacements for Claude models and deprecated request parameters.
sources.access: Public documentation. Its dates apply to Anthropic-operated platforms; partner platforms set their own schedules.
sources.reuse: Requests to a retired model fail. Test the recommended replacement on your own workload before the retirement date.

sources.name: OpenAI API pricing
sources.description: Provider prices by model and processing mode, including cached input, built-in tools, audio and image generation.
sources.access: Public pricing documentation. No paid model call is made by this collection.
sources.reuse: A calculated estimate is not an invoice. Recheck the exact model, processing mode, region and effective date.

sources.name: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.description: Announced retirements of OpenAI models and endpoints, with shutdown dates and recommended replacements.
sources.access: Public documentation. Notice periods differ by model type, and preview models can be retired with much shorter notice.
sources.reuse: A recommended replacement is the provider's suggestion, not a measured equivalent. Test it on your own task before the shutdown date.

sources.name: Gemini API pricing
sources.description: Free and paid tier prices for Gemini API models, including context caching, batch processing and search grounding.
sources.access: Public pricing documentation. An automated reader that does not keep cookies may be sent to a sign-in page instead.

sources.name: Gemini API deprecations
sources.description: Gemini API models with release dates, shutdown dates and recommended replacements.
sources.access: Public documentation for the Gemini API. Check the schedule of any other Google platform you use separately.
sources.reuse: A replacement model can differ in price, limits and behavior. Measure it on the same test set before the shutdown date.

sources.name: OpenRouter models API
sources.description: An endpoint listing models available through OpenRouter with per-token prices, context length, supported parameters and modalities.
sources.access: Follow the documented authentication and request limits. A listing shows routing availability, not access through your own provider accounts.
sources.reuse: One model can be served by several providers at different prices and limits. Record the provider, price basis and retrieval date with any figure.

sources.name: MCP specification changelog
sources.description: Changes in the current Model Context Protocol revision compared with the previous one, including breaking changes and deprecations.
sources.access: Public documentation. This address follows the latest revision; each revision also has its own dated page.
sources.reuse: The project is moving from the MIT licence to Apache-2.0; read its licence file before copying specification text. A published revision does not mean your SDK or host supports it yet.

sources.name: MCP Python SDK releases
sources.description: Tagged releases and change notes for the official MCP Python SDK.
sources.access: Read the release notes on GitHub, or use the GitHub Releases API with its request limits.
sources.reuse: MIT-licensed. Pin the version and run server and client tests before upgrading, especially across a major version.

sources.name: MCP TypeScript SDK releases
sources.description: Tagged releases and change notes for the official MCP TypeScript SDK.
sources.access: Read the release notes on GitHub, or use the GitHub Releases API with its request limits.
sources.reuse: The repository licence file describes a move from MIT to Apache-2.0. Pin the package version and run an integration test before upgrading.

sources.name: OpenAI Agents SDK releases
sources.description: Tagged releases and change notes for OpenAI's Agents SDK for Python.
sources.access: Read the release notes on GitHub, or use the GitHub Releases API with its request limits.
sources.reuse: MIT-licensed. The project is still before version 1.0, so read each release note for breaking changes before upgrading.

sources.name: Claude Agent SDK for Python releases
sources.description: Tagged releases and change notes for Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK for Python.
sources.access: Read the release notes on GitHub, or use the GitHub Releases API with its request limits.

sources.name: LangGraph releases
sources.description: Tagged releases for LangGraph and related packages, including its CLI, SDK and checkpoint libraries.
sources.access: Read the release notes on GitHub. One releases page covers several packages, so match the package name in each tag.
sources.reuse: MIT-licensed. Pin each package version separately and test saved checkpoints before upgrading.

sources.name: Pydantic AI releases
sources.description: Tagged releases and change notes for the Pydantic AI agent framework.
sources.access: Read the release notes on GitHub. Pre-releases and fixes for an older major version appear beside current stable releases.
sources.reuse: MIT-licensed. Use a stable release for production and test structured outputs and tool calls before upgrading.

sources.name: Claude Code changelog
sources.description: Version-by-version changes to Claude Code, generated from the changelog in its public repository.
sources.access: Public documentation. The page is long; read only the entries between the pinned and target versions.
sources.reuse: Claude Code is proprietary. Its repository states that use is subject to Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service.

sources.name: OpenAI Codex CLI releases
sources.description: Tagged releases of OpenAI's open-source Codex command-line coding agent.
sources.access: Read the release notes on GitHub. Alpha pre-releases appear beside stable releases.
sources.reuse: Apache-2.0 licensed. Using OpenAI models through it is governed by OpenAI's terms.

sources.name: OpenCode releases
sources.description: Tagged releases of the open-source OpenCode coding agent.
sources.access: Read the release notes on GitHub. Older links under the sst organization redirect to this repository.
sources.reuse: MIT-licensed. Model access is configured separately and governed by each provider's terms.

sources.name: Gemini CLI release notes
sources.description: Release notes for Google's open-source Gemini CLI across its stable, preview and nightly channels.
sources.access: Public documentation on the site that the project's GitHub repository lists as its homepage. The project recommends the stable channel for general use.
sources.reuse: Apache-2.0 licensed. Using Gemini models through it is governed by Google's terms.

sources.name: Cursor changelog
sources.description: Dated release notes for the Cursor editor and its agent features.
sources.access: Public page. This collection does not install, configure or sign in to the editor.
sources.reuse: Cursor is proprietary software. Check its terms and data settings before standardizing a team on a version.

sources.name: Aider release history
sources.description: Release history of the open-source aider terminal coding assistant, including unreleased changes on its main branch.
sources.access: Public page. Check the date of the newest release before assuming active maintenance.
sources.reuse: Apache-2.0 licensed. Model access is configured separately and governed by each provider's terms.

sources.name: OSV API
sources.description: Queries for known open-source vulnerabilities by package version, commit or advisory identifier, with a batch endpoint.
sources.access: Public API documentation. Its FAQ says the API currently has no rate limits; use batch queries for long dependency lists.
sources.reuse: OSV aggregates records from many source databases, each with its own licence listed on the OSV data page. Keep the advisory ID and fixed version with each finding.

sources.name: GitHub global security advisories API
sources.description: Endpoints for listing and reading GitHub Advisory Database entries, filtered by ecosystem, affected package and advisory type.
sources.access: Use the documented API with its authentication and request limits. Malware advisories are excluded unless requested.
sources.reuse: GitHub publishes the advisory data under CC BY 4.0 in a public repository. Distinguish reviewed advisories from unreviewed ones in any report.

sources.name: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
sources.description: Vulnerabilities that CISA lists as known to be exploited, with dates added, remediation due dates, required actions and ransomware-use flags.
sources.access: Public catalog with CSV and JSON downloads and a JSON schema. Its due dates apply to US federal civilian agencies, not to other organizations.
sources.reuse: Absence from the catalog does not make a vulnerability safe to ignore. Match the exact product and version before acting on an entry.

sources.name: Godot Engine documentation
sources.description: The official manual and class reference for the Godot 2D and 3D game engine, including scripting and export guides.
sources.access: Public documentation. The stable and latest branches can differ; select the one that matches the engine version in use.
sources.reuse: The engine is MIT-licensed and the documentation is CC BY 3.0. Plugins, assets and templates keep their own licences.

sources.name: Godot download archive
sources.description: Every official Godot release, including development, pre-release and release-candidate builds, with links to release news and changelogs.
sources.access: Read the news and changelog for the exact build. This collection downloads nothing.
sources.reuse: Treat development and pre-release builds as test material. Back up a project before opening it in a newer engine version.

sources.name: Blender release notes
sources.description: Release notes for each Blender version, including long-term support releases, with links to detailed notes such as Python API changes.
sources.access: Public pages. The detailed notes and the Python API reference are on Blender's developer and documentation sites, which can show a browser check to automated readers.
sources.reuse: Blender is GPL software, and Blender states that published scripts using its Python API must use a GPL-compatible licence.

sources.name: Babylon.js documentation
sources.description: Guides, API reference, what's new and breaking changes for the Babylon.js web rendering engine.
sources.access: Public documentation. Read the breaking changes page before moving a project to a new major version.
sources.reuse: The documentation states that its code samples are Apache 2.0 unless otherwise stated. Check the terms of models and textures separately.

sources.name: Babylon.js releases
sources.description: Tagged Babylon.js releases with change notes from the official repository.
sources.access: Read the release notes on GitHub, or use the GitHub Releases API with its request limits.
sources.reuse: Apache-2.0 licensed. Pin the package version and compare rendered output before upgrading a published scene.

sources.name: Blender Lab MCP Server
sources.description: Blender Lab's MCP server and add-on, which give an MCP client a natural-language interface to a Blender session through Blender's Python API.
sources.access: Requires Blender 5.1 or newer, the add-on, an MCP client and the server. Blender warns that it runs model-generated code without guards and recommends a virtual machine or a system without sensitive data.
sources.reuse: An official origin does not make generated code safe. Keep private files and credentials out of reach of the Blender session.

sources.name: MCP for Blender (community project)
sources.description: A widely used community MCP server and Blender add-on, not affiliated with the Blender Foundation. Its tools run arbitrary Python in Blender and fetch assets from external services.
sources.access: Third-party code that Baltor has not reviewed. Its README says a minimal anonymous usage record is sent by default and documents how to turn telemetry off.
sources.reuse: MIT-licensed code. Fetched assets keep their providers' terms, and several services need their own API keys or a paid plan.

sources.name: Godot MCP (community project)
sources.description: A widely used community MCP server for Godot, published outside the Godot project, that launches the editor, runs projects, captures debug output and edits scenes.
sources.access: Third-party code that Baltor has not reviewed. Its example client setup pre-approves tools that run projects and save scenes; review that list before use.
sources.reuse: MIT-licensed. Check recent repository activity and test against the Godot version in use before relying on it.

sources.name: MCP security best practices
sources.description: The protocol project's guidance on attacks and mitigations for MCP clients and servers, including local server compromise, token passthrough and server-side request forgery.
sources.access: Public documentation. This address follows the latest specification revision; earlier revisions have dated pages.
sources.reuse: Guidance is not an audit. Apply it to the exact server, transport and client configuration in use.

collections.title: Choose a coding model
collections.purpose: Compare coding evaluations before choosing a model and harness for repository work.
collections.agent_task: Prepare a source-linked comparison for the same evaluation setting. Separate publisher-reported results from results we reproduced; leave incompatible settings side by side without a combined rank.
collections.decision_question: Which model and harness combination should handle this repository task?
collections.review_trigger: Before changing the coding model or harness, or after a relevant evaluation or repository requirement changes.

collections.title: Review RAG and retrieval quality
collections.purpose: Choose what to measure when improving search, embeddings, reranking and grounded answers.
collections.agent_task: Propose a retrieval comparison on a fixed corpus, then a separate answer-quality check. Explain which public benchmark resembles the task and which differences need a local test.
collections.decision_question: Should we change the retriever, embeddings, reranker or answer-generation step?
collections.review_trigger: Before redesigning retrieval, after a corpus or query change, and when observed answer quality declines.

collections.title: Compare model cost and latency
collections.purpose: Estimate the cost of a workload and inspect measured latency under stated conditions.
compare_fields: time to first token and throughput
price date and measured versus estimated cost
collections.agent_task: Make a cost worksheet for the supplied workload. Cite the provider's current price, show token and cache assumptions, and keep estimated spend separate from reported usage and observed invoices.
collections.decision_question: Which provider and model meet the workload's quality, latency and spending constraints?
collections.review_trigger: At initial architecture review, after pricing or traffic changes, and during scheduled cost reviews.

collections.title: Review model safety and reliability
collections.purpose: Inspect a model's evaluated risks and the gaps that matter for a proposed use.
collections.agent_task: Summarize the evaluated risks for the specified task with exact source references. Do not turn a score into a guarantee; list the missing conditions and an appropriate independent test.
collections.decision_question: What evaluated risks remain for this model in the proposed use?
collections.review_trigger: Before a new use case or model release, and when incidents or new evaluation evidence change the risk assessment.

collections.title: Run models on your hardware
collections.purpose: Plan a model configuration that fits available memory and can be measured on the actual machine.
collections.agent_task: Separate memory estimates from measured compatibility. Propose a bounded benchmark using the exact hardware, model variant, context and runtime; do not claim a fit from parameter count alone.
collections.decision_question: Which exact model configuration fits the machine and meets the required throughput?
collections.review_trigger: Before choosing hardware or deploying a model, and after model, context, concurrency or runtime changes.

collections.title: Track model prices and retirements
collections.purpose: Catch price changes, new models and retirement dates before they force a rushed model switch.
compare_fields: quality and cost measured on our own test set
collections.agent_task: Check the named providers for price changes, new models and retirement notices that affect the current configuration. Cite each provider page with the date it was read, keep listed prices separate from observed invoices, and propose a side-by-side test before any switch.
collections.decision_question: Should we keep, re-price or replace the current model after a price change, release or retirement notice?
collections.review_trigger: When a provider announces a price change, model release or retirement, and before each budget review.

collections.title: Assess a model release
collections.purpose: Find model changes relevant to a task, then check access, licence and integration requirements.
collections.agent_task: Review the chosen publishers for relevant releases. Link the model card and exact revision, distinguish author claims from independent measurements, and identify a small compatibility test.
collections.decision_question: Does a new model offer enough relevant benefit to justify an integration test?
collections.review_trigger: When a chosen publisher releases a model or changes access, licence, support or deployment requirements.

collections.title: Choose MCP tools and services
collections.purpose: Discover services an agent can connect to and inspect permissions before enabling them.
collections.agent_task: Build a shortlist for the named task. Cite each server's official documentation, show required access and possible effects, and flag breaking changes without installing or connecting automatically.
collections.decision_question: Which service supplies the required capability with acceptable permissions and maintenance?
collections.review_trigger: Before enabling a server, after a protocol or authentication change, and during periodic access reviews.

collections.title: Turn papers into practical tests
collections.purpose: Find research that may improve a specific workflow and turn its claims into a reproducible test plan.
collections.agent_task: Find papers for the supplied problem and explain the practical method in original words. Link the exact version, note conflicting evidence and outline a test before recommending an implementation.
collections.decision_question: Which published method could improve this problem, and what would establish that it works here?
collections.review_trigger: During initial design, when a measured bottleneck appears, and when new evidence challenges the chosen method.

collections.title: Pick a founder stack
collections.purpose: Compare a small operating stack against a startup's workload, budget and migration needs.
collections.agent_task: Compare two workable stacks for the supplied constraints. Assign one owner to login, email, compute and storage; cite current limits and explain what remains custom. Do not create accounts or spend money.
collections.decision_question: Which email, login, compute and storage choices fit the product and its operating budget?
collections.review_trigger: At initial design and during reviews of cost, reliability, customer requirements or migration needs.

collections.title: Plan platform and tool upgrades
collections.purpose: Find relevant releases, breaking changes and deprecations for a chosen technology stack.
collections.agent_task: Review only the named dependencies and services. Separate a release announcement from a verified installation, and produce a change list with source links, applicability and a test or rollback step.
collections.decision_question: Which announced changes require action in this stack, and which can wait?
collections.review_trigger: When a tracked dependency releases or deprecates a feature, and before a scheduled maintenance window.

collections.title: Upgrade an agent framework
collections.purpose: Find breaking changes in agent frameworks, SDKs and the MCP specification before upgrading a working system.
compare_fields: integration test result and rollback version
collections.agent_task: Compare the pinned version with the target release for each named package. Link the relevant release notes, separate stable releases from pre-releases, and list the integration tests to run before upgrading. Do not install or upgrade anything.
collections.decision_question: Is this framework or SDK upgrade worth an integration test now, or can it wait?
collections.review_trigger: When a pinned framework, SDK or MCP revision publishes a release, and before you update dependencies.

collections.title: Standardize a coding agent version
collections.purpose: Choose which coding agent and version a team should run, and see what changed since the pinned one.
collections.agent_task: Summarize changes between the team's pinned version and the newest stable release of each named harness. Flag changes to defaults, permission prompts, sandboxing and supported models, then propose a short trial on a real repository task before standardizing.
collections.decision_question: Which harness and version should the team standardize on, and what changed since the pinned one?
collections.review_trigger: When a harness the team uses publishes a stable release, and before changing the team's standard setup.

collections.title: Check dependencies for advisories
collections.purpose: Find published vulnerabilities that affect the packages, tools and MCP servers an agent setup depends on.
collections.agent_task: Check the supplied dependency list against the advisory sources. Report exact matches with advisory links and fixed versions, mark uncertain matches, and propose the smallest safe update with a test. Do not change dependencies.
collections.decision_question: Does a published advisory affect a dependency we run, and how soon must we act?
collections.review_trigger: Before a release, after adding a dependency or MCP server, and when an advisory source publishes a matching entry.

collections.title: Choose a 3D or game engine
collections.purpose: Compare engines and 3D tools a creative agent can build on, using their own documentation and release notes.
compare_fields: licence for engine, scripts and assets
collections.agent_task: Compare the named engines for the supplied project. Cite official documentation for scripting, export and platform support, note version-specific limits, and propose a small prototype that tests the riskiest requirement. Do not install or download anything.
collections.decision_question: Which engine or tool should a creative agent build this project on?
collections.review_trigger: At project start, before a major engine upgrade, and when a required platform or export format changes.

collections.title: Connect creative tools through MCP
collections.purpose: Decide which MCP connection to a 3D tool is acceptable to enable, and under what isolation.
compare_fields: publisher and official or community status
collections.agent_task: Compare the named servers for the creative task. Show which tools can run code, write files or reach external services, and recommend an isolated setup such as a virtual machine. Do not install, connect or pre-approve tools.
collections.decision_question: Which MCP connection to this creative tool is acceptable to enable, and with what isolation?
collections.review_trigger: Before enabling a server, after a server or protocol update, and before the project handles private files.

collections.title: Track competitors and useful tools
collections.purpose: Find products that solve a named problem, then verify the claims at their own documentation.
collections.agent_task: Prepare a problem-based shortlist with primary product links and explicit unknowns. Do not equate launch popularity with usefulness or collect Product Hunt commercially without recorded permission.
collections.decision_question: Should we build, buy or reposition after comparing products that address this customer problem?
collections.review_trigger: During product positioning, before building a major feature, and when a relevant competitor changes its offering.

collections.title: Find a fitting hackathon
collections.purpose: Find events that match a project and check whether a reusable public demonstration is allowed.
collections.agent_task: Shortlist events for the stated skills, location and schedule. Verify each deadline and rule on the organizer's page; distinguish an eligible opportunity from a submitted application.
collections.decision_question: Which event fits our project, eligibility and ability to publish the intended demonstration?
collections.review_trigger: Before committing project time, and again when event rules or submission deadlines change.

collections.title: Research market explanations
collections.purpose: Research public filings and economic releases that may explain a market event.
collections.agent_task: Build a dated source trail for the supplied event. Keep alternative explanations and missing market data visible. Do not infer trader identity, confirmed rolls or profitable signals from public context alone.
collections.decision_question: Which public events could explain the observed market activity, and which explanations remain unsupported?
collections.review_trigger: After a supplied market event or relevant filing or economic release, with event time and data vintage preserved.
